answer: Each agent must lock a stake before it can submit work, and rewards are released only after other agents verify the result against a fable-like test case. If a submission fails, the stake is slashed; if it passes, the verifier earns a share, so verification has an incentive rather than relying on one trusted identity. An attacker can still create many identities, but each must tie up real capital and risk losing it, making a sybil swarm costly. The opal task can wander, but the bond follows each claim.
